Let your light shine
A very warm welcome to
Trent Young's
Thank you for your interest in our school. We hope that you will find our website both interesting and informative, as well as giving a taste for what is important to us at our school.
Here at Trent, our vision, 'to let your light shine' means that our priority is for each child to flourish: to believe in themselves, to understand the impact that they can have on each other, and to be happy and healthy. We believe that is it vital that each child understands how special, unique, and valued they are and is able to make a positive contribution to our school and the wider community. Our curriculum is designed to provide all children with the best possible opportunities to experience success, and to become curious individuals who care for each other and our world.

Don't forget that it's the Queen Thorne Garden Show on Saturday! There is artwork that has been produced by children from across the school displayed there and, there are still prizes up for grabs for the largest geraniums that the children brought home earlier in the year (these can be dropped off between 8am and 10am at Trent Memorial Hall for judging). It would be great to see the school represented brilliantly as we know lots of the geraniums were looking fantastic! #LetYourLightShine
What a performance of Oliver Jr our amazing KS2 children put on earlier in the month! They all wowed us with their performances and we know we have some budding theatre stars in our midst! Thank you so much to Sherborne Boys for allowing us to perform in the wonderful Big School Room, to all of our fantastic audience members, and to all of the adults at home who helped learn lines, rehearse songs and source costumes! #LetYourLightShine
What an incredible adventure our Year 5 and 6 classes had at the Weymouth Outdoor Education Centre. The children took on a brilliant mix of outdoor activities, including rock climbing, tunnelling, traverse climbing and a short drive to a beautiful nearby cove for some mega paddleboarding. Thank you to all the children for their bravery, cooperation, wonderful teamwork and endless enthusiasm. You represented the school beautifully and did us all proud! #LetYourLightShine
Fox and Owl Classes had an eye-opening and action-packed trip to the Carymoor Environmental Trust as part of our geography unit on climate change and sustainability! We walked through a waste tunnel and explored rubbish through the decades. It reminded us about why the 3Rs (Reduce, Reuse, Recycle) is so important. We also had a site tour, walking along their capped landfill with many layers of rubbish underneath the ground and visited the waste transfer station to see and learn that landfill sent here is incinerated to create electricity for thousands of houses! The children also played team building games by trying to dispose of toxic waste as well as comparing test tubes of rubbish and deciding on its impact on our planet. The trip was a powerful, hands-on reminder of exactly why the 3 Rs (Reduce, Reuse, Recycle) are so incredibly important for our future! #LetYourLightShine
Y6 Okehampton Day 2 What an amazing day! The children haven't stopped and have had the best time. Thankfully, it's been cooler than it has been back at school but we've still found every bit of shade we have been able to. It has still been very warm but the children have been fantastic and have been so supportive to each other! After a full, cooked breakfast, we were straight into grass sledging and axe throwing (yes, real, proper axes!) before then heading back into lunch. Climbing was the theme after lunch as we conquered both the high ropes course and the climbing wall before pizza and sticky toffee pudding at dinner. Finally, we've been doing archery and the blind trail - another first for a lot of us! It's much quieter this evening with almost all rooms now quiet and asleep ready for packing, breakfast and our cycle tour in the morning. #LetYourLightShine Adventure Okehampton
Day 1 at Adventure Okehampton It's been a very warm day but the children have coped brilliantly and have all had an amazing time. Having settled in and found their rooms, they were thrown straight into action as we headed to Meldon Gorge for a spot of gorge scrambling. The cold water was a very welcome relief and we had saw lots of jumping in, splashing and fantastic teamwork. Having enjoyed a lovely chicken pie and chocolate brownie, we've had a gentle evening with games being played, a bit of football on the TV and finished a bit of an Oliver sing-a-long! Mrs Thomson, Miss Hamm and Mr Hamblin are currently sat in the landing waiting for the last few voices to drift off to sleep. We've got a very busy day planned tomorrow with high ropes, grass sledging, archery, axe throwing and the climbing wall all in the mix! #LetYourLightShine
Well done to our amazing KS2 athletics team who competed in the Sherborne Area athletics meet yesterday afternoon. The children took part in a range of running events, long jump and throwing with great enthusiasm. We were pleased to see so many children keen to take part, managed some 1st, 2nd and 3rd place finishes, and also came 3rd out of 8 schools in the relay! #LetYourLightShine
Our Year 6s represented us brilliantly this morning as they joined children from the rest of our Diocese of Salisbury Academy Trust family for their leavers' service. They braved the rain and enjoyed the service that explored the theme of taking our 'light' with us as we embark on new ventures. They listened very attentively and sang wonderfully (including with lots of actions and clapping where necessary!). Thank you to both Diocese of Salisbury Academy Trust and Diocese of Salisbury for their work in putting the event together. #LetYourLightShine
We've had a great sports day which saw all children competing in their colour teams under the wonderful sunshine! Starting the day with field events, the children took part in events such as the obstacle course, welly wanging and the sack race. This was followed by all children taking part in a sprint in their year groups before a toddlers' race, parents' race, and the relays. It was great to see so many of you there supporting and thank you to the Friends of Trent School for their refreshments! A special well done to blue team for winning the event and being presented with our new sports day trophy for the first time! #LetYourLightShine
Yesterday saw 21 of our amazing Trent Young's students running in the Mini London Marathon!! After a quick warmup with Gladiators stars Jodie Ounsley and Harry Aikines-Aryeetey, we were out onto the streets of London with around 1000 other children from across the country. It was a very warm afternoon but that didn't stop the children from heading off at a blistering pace and they were on The Mall before they knew it! Along the whole route, the streets were lined with supporters cheering everyone on and thank you to all of the parents who came to support us too! As you can see from the pictures, they had a fantastic time and, we think we've been caught on camera as part of the BBC Sport highlights of the event too!! #LetYourLightShine #londonmarathon #MiniLondonMarathon
Wow!! What an utterly fantastic day we've had in London taking part in the Mini London Marathon In really warm conditions, the children excelled themselves and had a brilliant time. All of our runners made it over the line with huge smiles on their faces and were awarded with an amazing medal for their efforts. I'll get some photos on here tomorrow but, in the meantime, try to spot our Trent Team in the live stream below! Our runners start coming in from 12.48.40 on the clock on the finish line (approx. 04.33.40 in the video). #LetYourLightShine
Welcome to our September 2026 Starters We are delighted to welcome our new September 2026 starters and their families to the Trent Young's CE School community. Beginning school is an exciting and important step, and we are so pleased to be starting this journey with you. We are really looking forward to getting to know you and supporting your children as they take their first steps into school life. Our transition activities are designed to help children feel happy, secure and excited about joining our school family. Further information about transition arrangements and key dates will be shared soon, so please keep an eye out. We look forward to working together and watching your child's light shine brightly at Trent Young's CE School. #LetYourLightShine
On Friday, we had a fabulous morning in the sunshine on our spring walk. We were lucky to be able to get out to learn more about the signs of spring, the impact of the wet winter and how farmers are managing this. Thank you so much to Mr and Mrs Casely for leading our walk and for sharing their knowledge. Thank you to our amazing adult helpers for joining us for the morning too! #LetYourLightShine The Ernest Cook Trust
KS1 Trip to The Sealife Centre! What a fantastic day we had exploring life under the sea at Weymouth SEA LIFE Adventure Park! The children loved discovering all the incredible underwater creatures and learning how some of the animals are specially adapted to their habitats. The sunshine made the day even more magical, and Mr Squibb and Mrs Green were incredibly proud of the children - not just for their curiosity and enthusiasm, but also for their excellent behaviour throughout the trip. Well done KS1you were amazing! #LetYourLightShine

Welcome
A very warm welcome to Trent Young's CE School.
Thank you for your interest in our school. I hope that you will find our website both interesting and informative, as well as giving a taste for what is important to us at our school.
Here at Trent, our vision, 'to let your light shine' means that our priority is for each child to flourish: to believe in themselves, to understand the impact that they can have on each other, and to be happy and healthy. We believe that is it vital that each child understands how special, unique, and valued they are and is able to make a positive contribution to our school and the wider community. Our curriculum is designed to provide all children with the best possible opportunities to experience success, and to become curious individuals who care for each other and our world.
We look upon education as the lighting of a fire and our aim is to equip our children with the skills to succeed in life in the 21st century, both on an academic and a personal level. Children achieve when they are inspired and motivated, and we support this philosophy by providing a wide and balanced range of opportunities within a caring and secure learning environment.
We believe that in order for a child to achieve they need to have the confidence and security to try new things and to be open to many possibilities. A strong partnership between the school, parents, children, the church and the Diocese of Salisbury Academy Trust supports pupils at Trent to develop a positive attitude to learning.
You are welcome to make a personal visit to our school to see how we work and experience our ethos. If you would like to take the opportunity to do so, then please contact the school to arrange a time when we can show you around.
I look forward to meeting you and your children.

Wraparound Care
Trent Young's run Wraparound Care (Breakfast Club and an After School Care) service, which all children who are at school on a full time basis are welcome to attend.
Breakfast Club runs Monday - Friday from 07:30 - 08:20, when the children are escorted to their classrooms and includes breakfast.
After School Care runs from Monday - Friday from 15:00 to 17:30 and is charged at an hourly rate, with half hour slots available from 15:00 - 15:30 and 17:00 - 17:30. The children are provided with light healthy refreshments while they attend After School Care.
These services are run by qualified staff at the school, where children are cared for in a creative and fun environment and take part in activities such as art and craft, games and puzzles in the evenings, and quieter activities such as reading and lego in the mornings.
Bookings are made through Arbor, our online payment system. Please contact the school office or Wraparound care for further details if required, and any Wraparound Care queries can be emailed to wraparoundcare@trentyoungs.dsat.org.uk

Curriculum
The Curriculum at Trent
At Trent Young's we carefully plan our learning to ensure that each child receives a rich and balanced curriculum that enables them to flourish both academically and personally. Through the learning experiences provided, we aim to develop knowledge and understanding of the subjects taught; respect for each other, cultural diversity and the world in which we live; and an understanding of fundamental British values. For more details, please click on the links below, or come in to see us!
To find out more about the curriculum we follow, please click on the links below, or talk to your child's class teacher.
Our Approach to the Curriculum
Our Approach to the Curriculum
Let your Light Shine
Our Approach to the Curriculum
Our approach to the curriculum is firmly rooted in our vision: ‘Let your Light Shine’
Curriculum planning is accessible and relevant to all pupils, and covers the content of the National Curriculum. Through carefully sequenced lessons, children learn and apply a range of knowledge and concepts across all subjects. They also develop skills such as questioning, presenting, debating, making choices about their own learning and critically reflecting on their work, and that of their peers. We have five key themes which drive our curriculum: Health, Language, Community, Environment and Technology. (See our ‘Curriculum Drivers’ document for more details.) We use these 'drivers' to underpin the development work we undertake in all areas of school life and to ensure our curriculum offer is enriched and personalised to our children and their families.
Planning starts from the subject requirements (see individual subject documents for more detail) and meaningful links are then made within that subject, and with subjects. Teaching and learning in this way allows well-organised cross-curricular links to be made, which enable children to make connections between their learning and so deepen their engagement and understanding. We plan opportunities for learning which promote problem solving, creativity and communication in a purposeful and supportive environment.
All class teachers are responsible for providing a curriculum that is suitable for all pupils in the class, including those with Special Educational Needs or Disabilities (SEND) with support from the SENDCo. We have high expectations for all pupils and are committed to ensuring our curriculum complies with the Equality Act 2010, the SEND Code of Practice and the Special Educational Needs and Disability Regulations 2014. Our inclusion statement emphasises the importance of providing an inclusive learning environment for all pupils including those with SEND. Additional information on this can be found in our Special Education Needs Information Report and Equalities Policy.
Our behaviour policy ensures that our learning environment is positive and inclusive, enabling every child to make the most of the learning opportunities at our school. Children learn about the Protected Characteristics and Fundamental British Values to further develop their understanding of their roles and responsibilities in society.
The Extended Curriculum
We also believe that to truly flourish, children’s learning needs to go beyond the National Curriculum. We provide enrichment activities to enhance the curriculum, for example, the school organises themed days, linked to various aspects of the curriculum such as ‘positive relationships and anti-bullying week’; mental health and well-being; curriculum linked days or weeks; World Book Day; Children in Need day etc. We aim to provide a variety of extra-curricular activities for all children that will meet their needs, interests and enhance their skills and learning. These clubs are changed termly. (See PE grant document and Extra-Curricular page on our school website).

Our Curriculum Drivers
When designing our curriculum, we took into account the needs of our learners and community, our vision and values, and the location of our school. These ‘big ideas’ or curriculum drivers are used to underpin the development work we undertake in all areas of school life and to ensure our curriculum offer is enriched and personalised to our children and their families.
During their time at Trent Young’s, we want our children to develop habits and acquire knowledge and skills that will promote good health, both physical and mental. We want each child to have experiences which enable them to understand the importance of eating a balanced diet and getting regular exercise; to learn and apply strategies which will help them to deal with life experiences; and develop the ability to solve problems.

All of our children learn French; language learning from Reception sows the seeds of curiosity that enable children to learn about, and foster an interest in, another language and culture other than their own. As their curiosity blossoms so does their confidence, appetite for learning about other languages, countries, communities and cultures. Language learners use their skills to harvest vital knowledge and understanding that improves communication and literacy skills in their own language. We teach languages to broaden horizons and enhance future opportunities for study, work and travel as well as developing a lifelong passion for languages.
We believe that our curriculum will enable the children to develop the emotional understanding necessary to experience positive relationships, to develop a sense of justice and an ability to empathise, which in turn will lead to respect for themselves and each other. Inclusion Statement
At Trent Young’s CE School we work hard to ensure that every member of our school community – children, parents, staff, governors and visitors – feel safe and included. We are an inclusive school and every child, whatever their individual abilities or needs, is equally valued and welcome here. We expect each member of our community, staff, children, parents and visitors, to understand and support our inclusive ethos. We aim to create a happy, safe and secure environment, where members of our school community are healthy, enjoy learning, achieve their potential, respect and value each other and themselves.
As an educationally inclusive school the teaching and learning, achievements, attitudes and well-being of every young person matters. We take into account children’s varied life experiences and needs, providing equal opportunities for all pupils, whatever their age, disability, race, religion or belief, gender / gender identity or socio-economic background, to ensure that every child really does matter.
We aim to develop a culture of inclusion and diversity in which success is celebrated and all those connected to the school feel proud of their identity and able to participate fully in school life. We will tackle discrimination by the positive promotion of equality and the creation of an environment which champions respect for all.

We are part of the Operation Encompass Project, which is a partnership between schools and the police to support children who have experienced Domestic Violence.
WHAT WE DELIVER
Operation Encompass directly connects the police with schools to ensure support for children living with domestic abuse in their homes when there has been a police attended incident of Domestic Abuse. Rapid provision of support within the school environment means children are better safeguarded against the short-, medium- and long-term effects of domestic abuse.
WHAT WE DO
Operation Encompass provides an efficient, confidential channel of communication between police forces and Key Adults within schools. This enables the immediate and discrete recognition of the child's situation by the Key Adult, ensuring a secure and sympathetic environment is provided and the broader effects of abuse are addressed.
WHO WE ARE
Operation Encompass is a charitable organisation set up in 2011, which has since enabled effective interventions to many thousands of children who've experienced domestic abuse. The creators of Operation Encompass are working tirelessly to ensure that police and schools throughout the country are able to address victims of domestic abuse consistently and coherently.
